topics.topic: Whether an owner-only start opens or omits the service API listener
questions: Does this statement apply only when the service API is configured, or must an owner-only start also open a service API listener despite A17 rule 1 saying it opens none?
Does an owner-only start open a service API listener, as this passage says for each surface, or open no service API listener, as A17 rules 1 and 9 require?
Does an owner-only start omit the service API listener and its address, as A17 requires, or must Registry always serve both surfaces on configured listeners?

quotes:
Registry serves
each surface on a listener of its own, at its configured address, and
decides nothing about reachability beyond that listener's own form — bound
exclusively, an IPv6 one for IPv6 alone (A17 rule 1).

An owner-only start holds no
token and opens no service API, so no service call reaches it (A17 rule 1).
judgement.why: The unconditional requirement to serve each of the two surfaces on its own listener conflicts with the explicit owner-only rule that no service API is opened.

unsupported_sides:
Registry serves
each surface on a listener of its own, at its configured address, and
decides nothing about reachability beyond that listener's own form — bound
exclusively, an IPv6 one for IPv6 alone (A17 rule 1).

witness.initial: The owner-interface address and every other required owner setting are valid, while all four service tokens and the service API address are absent.
events: The host administrator starts Registry with this owner-only configuration.
Registry completes its checks and begins serving.
A service client attempts to connect to Registry's service API.
outcomes: The first passage requires Registry to serve the service API, one of its two surfaces, on its own configured listener.
The second passage requires Registry to open no service API, so the client's connection reaches no Registry.
witness.observer: The host administrator and the service client
basis:
the address the service API listens on, or, for an
   owner-only start, none of these five: Registry then serves the owner
   interface alone,
   opening no listener of the service API, so a service call reaches no
   Registry and is refused by its connection failing, with no answer (owner,
   2026-11-01; A18 rule 9).

Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
   names the failed item and never its value (R0-37).
